acceptance.assertion: The exact slice defines one provider_id github.public-rest with origin https://api.github.com and exactly one operation repository.read whose effect_class is read. Provider execution remains explicitly named by the caller; no select, route, rank, fallback, default or browser-worker start path is introduced anywhere in the slice.

The provider accepts no token, cookie, Authorization value, caller header map, browser profile or session identity. Only fixed non-secret provider-owned HTTP headers needed for the public GitHub API may be emitted. Tests prove unknown credential/header inputs are rejected or structurally impossible and no secret access surface is invoked.

Execution first reuses the existing StructuredToolProvider eligibility contract and then permits only canonical https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo> targets with bounded conservative owner/repository path segments. Query, fragment, userinfo, non-HTTPS, alternate origins, path traversal, empty/extra segments and redirects fail closed before a successful provider outcome.

A provider call performs at most one bounded anonymous HTTPS repository-metadata read with finite timeout and response-size limit. Success requires an expected JSON response and returns only an explicit bounded metadata projection plus digests/status; raw response body, arbitrary headers and unbounded provider data are never returned. Transport, HTTP, content-type, decode or bound violations fail closed with retry_authorized=false.

The real provider receipt is bound to provider ID, operation, existing read effect class, freshly resolved effect-contract digest and target digest, then normalized through the existing StructuredToolProvider normalize_receipt path. The provider creates no second Effect/Lifecycle/Retry authority; normalizer_execution_performed=false, automatic_route_selected=false, retry_authorized=false and authoritative_readback_required=true remain invariant.

Focused security/contract tests, py_compile/diff checks and the full relevant Grabowski validation are green on the exact PR head; normal GitHub required checks are green; after merge a fresh live anonymous call to the public heimgewebe/grabowski repository through this exact provider succeeds and its bounded normalized outcome is read back. No Grabowski runtime deploy or public capability exposure is claimed unless this slice actually changes a deployed runtime contract.

approval.note: The user explicitly continued the Browser Control Plane work. Scope is one tooling/core read-only public REST provider only. No credentials, browser action, router, public MCP/Grip exposure, default change, retry authority or backend promotion effect is authorized.

goal: Implement exactly one real, explicit, anonymous read-only StructuredToolProvider backend above the verified StructuredToolProvider contract. The backend is provider_id github.public-rest, declares only operation repository.read with the existing authoritative browser effect class read, accepts only canonical targets of the form https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>, performs one bounded anonymous HTTPS GET without caller-supplied headers, credentials, query or fragment, returns only a bounded selected repository-metadata projection plus a contract-bound provider receipt, and normalizes that receipt through the existing provider-neutral normalizer. This slice must not add automatic provider selection, ranking, fallback, default changes, browser-worker/session authority, credential/profile access, retry authority, MCP/Grip exposure or production router/promotion. After accepted live proof it counts as exactly one real backend; a router remains forbidden until at least two real revision-bound accepted backends exist.

metadata.architecture_position: First real StructuredToolProvider backend after the contract-only slice. It is intentionally anonymous/read-only and explicit-provider-only so execution semantics can be proven before any routing policy exists.

rollback.strategy: Revert only the GitHub provider source/tool/test/doc slice through a normal PR. The underlying StructuredToolProvider contract and semantic Browser Control Plane remain unchanged; no router/default/fallback is enabled by rollback.
